description: Cross-driver regression corpus for the hotstrings delay/color/show_tooltip resolution cascade (DL-5). Both drivers resolve each field independently through the SAME four levels, first non-empty wins: user_section > user_category > toml_section > toml_category > (driver-specific hardcoded default, already pinned identical by TestHotstringsConfig_SharedDefaultsAreSingleSource / test_hotstrings_defaults.lua — not re-tested here). Scope note: AHK's cascade also has a Priority field and a menu-set '_global' delay tier that macOS's hotstrings_config.lua does not implement; those are intentionally OUT OF SCOPE for this corpus (not asserted equal) — every vector below only ever sets delay/color/show_tooltip at the four genuinely shared levels, so both drivers reach an identical result via identical precedence. A level object is OMITTED entirely when not set for a vector; a field key inside a present level is OMITTED when that specific field is not set at that level (both mean 'fall through to the next level' for that field).

vectors.description: Only the category-level TOML _meta sets values; no section requested, no user override anywhere.
A [_meta.sections.<name>] entry wins over the file-level [_meta] when that section is requested.
A user file-level override wins over any TOML metadata, even with no section requested.
A user section-level override wins over user file-level, TOML section, and TOML file — the top of the cascade.

Each field resolves through the cascade on its own — delay from user_category (no user_section value for it), color from toml_section (no user value at any level), show_tooltip from toml_category (no toml_section value for it). Proves the cascade is per-field, not per-level.

The shared override file is case-insensitive for category identifiers: a mixed-case ext.<id> setter must resolve through an independently cased lookup, matching the Windows parser and writer contract.
